page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, consisting of 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 504 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 137 GB. No GPU accelerators are present, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of single-core efficiency and multi-core limitations. The instance achieves average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2240.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1858.0. Single-threaded text processing is highly efficient, ranking in the top tier with a score of 2828.0, and single-threaded gzip compression is strong at 35.55 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak. The stress-ng multi-core performance is 4549.86, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 4215.0, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read speeds registering at a poor 22.46 GB/sec and write speeds at a weak 15.13 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). These instructions assist in low-latency operations, as demonstrated by average performance in small-model LLM inference, where the 135M model processes prompts at 591.08 tokens/sec. However, larger models show steep performance degradation, with 7B model text generation dropping to a poor 5.04 tokens/sec. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local NVMe storage, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive, single-threaded tasks or lightweight database operations that do not saturate multi-core execution or memory bandwidth. Appropriate workloads include text processing, single-threaded data compression, Redis caching, and lightweight local database hosting.

While single-core performance is average, highlighted by top-tier single-threaded text processing and strong gzip compression, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth are weak, with large-block memory reads dropping to 22.46 GB/sec.
